Ground Operations & Rebooking Desk
Policy Extract: GO-RB-07, Rebooking Following Operational Disruption
Revision 4 (effective 1 September 2026)
Owner: Duty Operations Manager, Ground Operations

4. Rebooking Entitlements

4.1 Where a scheduled flight is cancelled or delayed by more than 150 minutes from its published departure time, the Rebooking Desk shall offer the affected passenger the next available seat on a Northmarsh service to the same destination, at no charge.

4.2 Offers under 4.1 shall be made within 60 minutes of the cancellation being recorded in the Flight Ops Log (FOL), or within 60 minutes of the passenger's first contact with the desk if later.

4.3 Where the next available seat departs more than 12 hours after the original departure time, the agent shall also offer a partner rebooking via Coastline Connect (contract ref. NRA/CC/2291), subject to the partner's seat availability at the time of offer.

4.4 Hotel accommodation is provided only where a passenger is stranded overnight at the departure station and no seat is available on any service departing before 09:00 the following day.

4.5 Exception. Clauses 4.1 to 4.4 do not apply to passengers travelling on a booking made through a third-party agent, which shall be referred to the Agency Liaison Team (extension 4417) before any offer is made. Where the Duty Operations Manager has authorised a waiver under 4.6, this exception does not apply.

4.6 The Duty Operations Manager may authorise a waiver of 4.3 or 4.4 where the disruption is caused by a documented safety or weather event at the departure station and the passenger has been notified before departure. Waivers shall be recorded in the FOL with the authorising initials and the time of authorisation.

5. Recording

5.1 Every rebooking offer, acceptance or refusal shall be logged against the booking reference within the same shift. Entries made after shift handover shall be marked "LATE" and initialled.

CASE NOTE: GO-RB-07 REF 26-1031-0412

Flight NR 3382, Northmarsh Regional, Stansbury to Carrowby, scheduled departure Saturday 31 October 2026 at 21:55, cancelled at 22:20 following a crew hours exceedance. Cancellation recorded in FOL at 22:34 by R. Pemberton.

Passenger contacted the desk at 23:40 on the same date. Booking is direct, reference KHVT7P, two adults, one infant. Passenger reports that the infant requires a seat with a bassinet and that the family cannot remain at Stansbury overnight.

Earliest seat offered on NR 3382 is Monday 2 November at 06:15, which is 32 hours 20 minutes after original departure. Coastline Connect has no seats on Sunday 1 November before 14:00. Passenger declined the Coastline option, stating the 14:00 connection would miss a pre-booked transfer at Carrowby.

Passenger has requested hotel accommodation for the night of 31 October. Desk notes no seat departs before 09:00 on 1 November on any Northmarsh service. Weather at Stansbury was reported as clear.

Offer status: open, pending duty manager review. Shift handover at 23:00 was not completed on this file.

Policy ref: HAS/POL/04 (v3.2)
Effective: 1 April 2026

4.1 Scope
4.1.1 This section applies to any client who has received a written notice from a private landlord seeking possession of a residential dwelling in England.
4.1.2 Advisers must record the date of service on the Notice Register before any further action is taken.

4.2 Arrears threshold
4.2.1 Where the notice cites rent arrears, the adviser must refer the case to the Tribunal Team if arrears at the date of service are £1,850.00 or more.
4.2.2 Where arrears are below £1,850.00, the adviser may proceed with a negotiated repayment plan without referral.
4.2.3 Arrears are calculated from the rent schedule on the tenancy agreement, less any payments received within the 14 days before service.

4.3 Exceptions
4.3.1 Clause 4.2.1 does not apply where the client is in receipt of a Discretionary Housing Payment award that has not yet been paid into the tenancy account. In such cases the adviser must note the award reference and refer to the Tribunal Team within 2 working days of payment.
4.3.2 Clause 4.3.1 does not apply where the landlord has issued a notice under Section 8 more than once in the preceding 12 months.

4.4 Record keeping
4.4.1 Calculations must show the working in the case file, including the rent schedule version used.

7.2 Hours are recorded to the nearest 0.25 hour. Hours under 0.125 past a quarter-hour boundary are rounded down.

7.3 Overtime is payable at 1.5 times basic hourly rate for hours exceeding 40.00 in a pay week, and at 2.0 times for hours on a Sunday or public holiday.

7.4 Exception: where a client has a signed variation on file (form CV-2), the threshold in 7.3 is the figure stated on that variation, provided the variation is dated on or before the pay week in question.

7.5 Corrections to a submitted timesheet must be logged on the Adjustment Register (ref. ADJ-) with the original and corrected figure, and countersigned by the client contact.

Ref: CBP-LVC-07 | Issue 4 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Entry Compliance

4.1 Scope
This clause applies to all import entries where the declared goods value does not exceed GBP 900.00 per consignment and the consignment is sent by a non-commercial shipper.

4.2 Valuation evidence
Entry clerks must obtain one of the following before release: (a) a commercial invoice showing shipper name, consignee name and currency; (b) a marketplace order confirmation with transaction reference; or (c) a signed shipper declaration on form HV-3.

4.3 Threshold referral
Where the declared value is GBP 850.00 or above, the entry must be referred to the Valuation Desk before release, regardless of evidence provided under 4.2.

4.4 Exception: family and gift consignments
Clause 4.3 does not apply where the shipper and consignee share a surname and the goods are identified on the shipper declaration as personal effects or gifts, provided the declaration is countersigned by the consignee.

4.5 Conflicting statements
Where the shipper and consignee give different accounts of the goods, the clerk must record both accounts on the entry file note and hold the consignment pending review. Neither account is to be treated as authoritative by default.

Operations Manual | Section 4: Food Temperature Records and Corrective Action
Document ref: OPS-HYG-04 | Version 3.2 | Issued: 2 March 2026 | Review: March 2027

4.1 Scope
This procedure applies to all Brindley & Vane sites operating chilled storage, hot holding or cooling of cooked product. It applies to Site Managers, Shift Leads and any member of kitchen staff recording temperatures.

4.2 Recording
4.2.1 Every temperature reading shall be entered on the Cooling and Holding Log (form CHL-2) at the time it is taken, and in any case within 30 minutes.
4.2.2 Readings must state the unit or equipment ID, the probe used (P1, P2 or P3) and the initials of the person taking the reading.
4.2.3 Corrections are made by a single line through the original entry, initialled and dated. Entries must not be erased.

4.3 Limits
4.3.1 Chilled storage must be at or below 5°C.
4.3.2 Cooked product being cooled must reach 8°C or below within 90 minutes of leaving the heat source, and 5°C or below within a further 210 minutes.
4.3.3 Hot holding must be at or above 63°C.

4.4 Corrective action
4.4.1 Where a reading breaches clause 4.3, the Shift Lead shall quarantine the affected product, label it HOLD, and inform the Site Manager immediately.
4.4.2 The Site Manager shall record the time of quarantine, the product affected and the action taken in Section C of the CHL-2.
4.4.3 A Corrective Action Report (form CAR-1) shall be sent to the Area Compliance Officer within three working days of the breach. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays.

4.5 Exceptions
4.5.1 Where a unit has been reported faulty and engineer attendance is pending, the Site Manager may authorise chilled product to be held at up to 8°C for no more than four hours, provided the product is not ready-to-eat and is discarded if the limit is exceeded.
4.5.2 An exception under 4.5.1 is valid only when the authorisation is written in Section D of the CHL-2 with the name, signature and time of the authorising manager.
4.5.3 An exception does not extend the CAR deadline in 4.4.3.

4.6 Retention
Completed CHL-2 and CAR-1 forms are retained on site for 12 months and then sent to the Area Compliance Officer for archive.
